admission.justification: The crossing keeps the standing of the selected content under both input orders.

applicability: An admitted crossing of two memory lines selecting or combining record meaning.
conditions: An input may lack a writer stamp, review evidence or both. The crossing preserves the selected content's writer stamp when available. Eligible unambiguous legacy standing can survive without usable exact reviewed-tree proof when the crossing introduces no different content at that revision number.
Same-number different content receives credit only for exact reviewed meaning.
exclusions: Only combined meaning that differs from both sides earns a new product stamp.

evidence: mcp/tests/test_worktree_sync_crossing_writer.py::test_crossing_preserves_the_standing_of_its_selected_bytes, archived prior-filename proof, and W10 expanded evidence.

statement: A crossing retains the selected record bytes and their admissible review facts. Equal bytes take standing from the merged histories. A genuinely combined revision receives the product stamp and derives state from ordinary history rules. Conflicting meaning fields remain conflicts.
